This is an opportunity for an experienced facilities, building maintenance, asset or trade professional to step into a broad supervisory role combining team leadership, maintenance planning, minor project delivery, contractor management and technical advice.

Reporting to the Coordinator Building Maintenance, you will lead the operational maintenance function and supervise the Facilities Operation Officer and Team Leader Operational Maintenance. You will coordinate reactive and preventative maintenance, minor capital and operational projects, and support the long-term performance of Council’s built assets.

  • Leading the delivery of minor capital and operational projects from scoping through to completion

  • Leading, motivating and developing staff while maintaining a strong safety, wellbeing and accountability culture
  
The position also participates in a rostered on-call function, with some out-of-hours work and domestic travel required.
  
About You
  
You will be a practical and organised maintenance or facilities professional who understands how to keep a diverse built asset portfolio operating safely, efficiently and reliably. Just as importantly, you will be comfortable leading people, coordinating competing priorities and working closely with contractors and internal stakeholders.
Council is open to candidates from facilities management, building maintenance, asset management, project delivery or relevant trade backgrounds.
  
You will bring:
  
  • Demonstrated experience delivering reactive and preventative maintenance across buildings or facilities
  • Experience scoping, planning, scheduling and delivering minor capital and operational projects
  • Strong contractor, trade and supplier management capability
  • Experience with building condition assessments, maintenance planning and asset renewal activities
  • The ability to read and interpret building plans, specifications and engineering reports
  • Sound knowledge of relevant building, fire safety and workplace health and safety requirements
  • Strong team leadership, communication, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills

A General Construction White Card and Queensland C Class Driver Licence, or interstate equivalent, are essential.

You will work across a diverse portfolio of community infrastructure and have the scope to improve maintenance planning, contractor performance, asset information and day-to-day service delivery.

community identity and easy access to beaches, national parks and the Whitsundays.

job.description:
Public Sector People are partnering with Clarence Valley Council to appoint a Coordinator – Building Services within the Development and Land Use Planning team.

Covering more than 10,000 square kilometres and serving a community of over 50,000 residents, Clarence Valley Council is one of the largest and most diverse regional councils in coastal NSW. From rural properties and villages through to Grafton, Yamba and Maclean, the Building Services team delivers a broad range of certification and assessment work across an extensive local government area.

Following a recent organisational restructure, this is an exciting opportunity to lead an established technical team while helping embed a more streamlined service model that allows Building Services to focus on certification, assessment and customer service.

About the Role
Reporting to the Manager Development and Land Use Planning, you'll lead a team of six registered Building Surveyors and a Building Inspector, providing leadership, technical guidance and operational oversight across Council's Building Services function.

The team delivers a broad range of certification and development assessment work, predominantly across residential development (Class 1 and 10), together with commercial, industrial and public infrastructure projects.

While you'll remain technically involved where required, your primary focus will be supporting the team, driving consistency in decision-making, improving customer service and continuing to strengthen operational practices.

Building Services is currently transitioning to a new operating model, with a dedicated Compliance team being established separately. This will allow the successful candidate to focus on leading the Building Services team while supporting the implementation of an improved organisational structure.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead, mentor and develop an experienced team of Building Surveyors and technical staff
  • Coordinate the delivery of certification, assessment and inspection services
  • Provide technical guidance on building legislation and certification matters
  • Promote consistency across decision-making, customer service and operational practices
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives across systems and service delivery
  • Build strong relationships with planners, developers, consultants and the community
  • Contribute to the ongoing development of the Building Services function during a period of positive organisational change
About You
You're a qualified Building Surveyor who enjoys supporting others and creating a positive, high-performing team environment.

You may already be leading a team, or you could be an experienced Senior Building Surveyor ready to take the next step into leadership.

We're interested in professionals who bring sound technical knowledge together with the ability to mentor staff, build relationships and continuously improve the way services are delivered.
You'll bring:
  • Registration with NSW Fair Trading (or eligibility for registration) as a: Building Surveyor Unrestricted (formerly A1) – preferred; Building Surveyor Restricted All Classes (formerly A2); or Building Surveyor Restricted (Class 1 and 10 Buildings) and actively progressing steps towards Unrestricted/Restricted All Classes registration.
  • Experience in building certification and development assessment
  • Strong understanding of NSW planning and building legislation
  • Leadership experience, or a demonstrated readiness to step into a leadership role
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
  • A collaborative, practical approach with a genuine interest in developing people and improving services
Why Join Clarence Valley Council?
  • Lead an experienced, technically capable Building Services team
  • Join the organisation during an exciting period of positive organisational change
  • Focus on certification and assessment within a streamlined operating model
  • Diverse mix of residential, commercial and industrial work
  • Opportunity to influence how the service continues to evolve
  • Strong regional network of building professionals
  • Flexible working arrangements with a 35-hour week and flex time
Salary & Benefits
  • $108,853 – $129,809 plus superannuation
  • Leaseback vehicle
  • Relocation assistance available
  • 35-hour week with flex time
  • My Leave provisions under the NSW Local Government Award
  • Fitness Passport
  • Ongoing professional development and training
Live and Work in the Clarence Valley
Whether you're already based in the Northern Rivers or looking for a lifestyle change, the Clarence Valley offers an enviable balance of career and lifestyle. With Grafton, Maclean and Yamba all within easy reach, you'll enjoy affordable living, stunning beaches, national parks and a welcoming regional community, while leading one of the region's key technical teams.
